title: icoSphere
body:
## icoSphere

Creates a closed sphere mesh by recursively subdividing an icosahedron with Blender's bmesh generator, giving near-uniform triangles with vertices on the given radius about centre. Choose it over uvSphere when even triangle size matters (wire cages, remeshing, deformation); subdivisions grows the face count by a factor of four per level.

Common mistakes and assumptions:

- Like uvSphere, the mesh is inscribed in the true sphere and slightly undersized in volume.
- The adaptor's recorded native qualification cases cover only a material on a cube; this operation relies on repository examples, not on a recorded qualification case.

Native binding: `icoSphere`. Output kind: `["data"]`.

| Input port | Multiplicity | Required | Kind |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `material` | one node | yes | `material` |

| Option | Meaning | Type / constraints | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `radius` | Radius of the sphere on which all vertices lie. | `{"type":"number","minimum":0,"exclusiveMinimum":true}` | `1` |
| `subdivisions` | Refinement level of the icosahedron: 1 is the plain 20-face icosahedron and each further level multiplies the triangle count by four (2 gives 80, 5 gives 5120). | `{"type":"integer","minimum":1,"maximum":5}` | `2` |
| `centre` | World position [x, y, z] of the sphere's centre. Schemaxis assigns it as the object's location, so the mesh itself stays about the local origin and later modifiers that work about that origin (mirror, bend, twist) use this point. | `{"type":"array","items":{"type":"number"},"minItems":3,"maxItems":3}` | `[0,0,0]` |
| `smoothShading` | When true, every face of the generated icoSphere is marked smooth so Blender interpolates normals and the tessellated surface renders without visible facets; when false the faces render flat. Geometry and vertex positions are identical either way. | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `false` |
